text.p: The Lebanese government said on Wednesday it plans to issue a $100 million eurobond to finance the reconstruction of its war-damaged electricity network.

"The finance ministry was instructed to prepare for a $100 million eurobond issue for (state-run utility) Electricite du Liban, with the World Bank as guarantor of the principal and the Lebanese government the interest," Information Minister Farid Makari told reporters after a cabinet session.

He said the plan -- which would be Lebanon's fourth foray into international capital markets -- was within the context of a draft law sent earlier to parliament allowing the government to borrow $365 million for rebuilding electricity stations and lines. Makari did not say when the issue will come out.

The Lebanese government in May issued a $100 million addition to a $300 million 9.125 percent eurobond issued in July 1995. The proceeds of the four-year issues were to be used to rebuild the infrastructure of villages damaged in the 1975-90 civil war.
Beirut's first highly successful venture into international capital markets was a $400-million three year eurobond, at 10.125 percent, in 1994 which was heavily oversubscribed.

Makari said the ministry of electricity plans to send a delegation for talks with the World Bank for a $65-million loan to finance the rebuilding of the electricity networks and major sub-stations in south and east Lebanon.

He said the government's reconstruction agency, the Council for Developement and Reconstruction (CDR), was also delegated to sign a $20.08 million loan deal with Paribas Capital Markets and another loan deal totalling $4.7 million with Beirut's Banque Saradar to help finance the construction of power lines.
